title: Kian's Folding Fun
markdown:
Kian loves measuring. He measures toast, crayons, even wiggly worms. Today, Kian and his friends had a very important job for the school fair: ribbons for the prize pies.

“They need to be exactly the same length,” Kian said. “Like twins!”

Lily agreed.

Kian took a red ribbon. Snip! But Puddle the frog hopped over with a blue one. “Mine is shorter?” he croaked sadly. Lily’s yellow ribbon was longer. Kian frowned. “This is harder than I thought!” The ribbons looked like a floppy noodle.

Suddenly Puddle ribbit-ed. “Look, Kian! Grandma Nell!”

Grandma Nell was in her garden, tucking in flowers. She took string from her pocket. She held it by a flower, then folded it in half. Ooooooh, whispered Kian. She folded it again and again. She used the folded string to show where each flower should go.

Kian’s eyes went wide. Grandma Nell was folding the string to make little bits that were all the same size. “Puddle! I know what to do!”

Kian grabbed more string. “Hold this, Puddle.” Puddle held it tight. Kian took the other end. He folded the string so the ends met. “Two equal parts!” he whispered.

“Ribbit! Two equal parts!” Puddle wiggled his nose.

“But we need smaller parts!” Kian said, his brain doing happy flips. He folded the string in half again. And again. “Now we have four equal parts! This is our perfect ribbon length!”

Using the folded string as a guide, Kian and Puddle started again. Kian made a crease on the ribbon. Puddle nudged it. Snip went Kian’s scissors. Snip! Snip! Snip! Each ribbon was cut perfectly. Every single one was exactly the same. Yay!

Grandma Nell came inside. “My goodness, Kian! How did you make them all the same?”

Kian beamed. “I learned to measure by folding, Grandma Nell. When you fold something so the ends meet, you make two equal halves. You can fold again and again to make smaller equal parts.”

Puddle gave a happy ribbit that sounded like a giggle. “Folding makes them all the same!”

Grandma Nell smiled. “That’s right, Kian. By folding, you discovered how to divide things into equal lengths. It’s a wonderful way to make sure things are just right.”

The prize-pie ribbons lay in a neat twin-stack, red and blue and yellow, all matching. Lily held one up next to Puddle’s. Same. Kian tucked the folded string into his pocket, a little ruler made of creases, ready for the fair.
characters: Kian (measure master), Puddle (frog), Grandma Nell (grandmother), Lily (friend)
author: StoryGen Community
